Thanks a lot for tackling this @anatawa12.

Some high level comments/questions about the implementation:
1. `Microsoft.NET.HostModel` already depends on `System.Reflection.Metadata`. There seems to be quite some overlap between the functionality being pulled into `Mono.Cecil.Binary` and what is already provided in [`System.Reflection.PortableExecutable`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.reflection.portableexecutable) - specifically [`PEReader`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.reflection.portableexecutable.pereader).
    - Could this use the reading functionality available in `System.Reflection.Metadata` instead?
2. The runtime repo has some code used by other tools to read resource data into a model and update it: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/coreclr/tools/Common/Compiler/Win32Resources
    - Could this re-use that resource data model instead?

In general, I'm looking to re-use existing code/functionality and pull in as little new logic as possible that we would have to ship in the SDK and maintain separately from other implementations. I think if the two things above are doable, it would just leave the actual writing/patching as new logic specific to HostModel.

Testing is probably my biggest concern here. This basically affects every build targeting Windows. Unfortunately, even running on Windows, we have a significant test hole around resource updating.

With the exception of those two tests, that were failing and you addressed, the tests in the runtime repo aren't actually using `ResourceUpdater` (if they were, I expect more tests would have failed). There is one [test in dotnet/sdk](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/f11a8e48cfe0dc7af957eca21f4fde89bf793573/src/Tests/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tests/AppHostTests.cs#L301) that explicitly targets resources being copied from the managed dll, but that would only catch failures when we try to integrate runtime into sdk, rather than when the changes are made in runtime.

Ideally, we would have:
- Unit tests for `ResourceUpdater`
  - Something basic like updating and reading it back to check that a resource was added
- Integration tests using `HostModel` to update an apphost
  - Most tests in this repo don't actually go through `HostWriter`/`ResourceUpdater` and the ones that do actually don't pass in a binary from which to copy resources. I'm going to look into this - this was a surprise to me and we need to fix it.
- E2E tests for cross-building an app on Unix targeting Windows
  - I don't think we really have a good mechanism for doing this in runtime. I believe the sdk repo has some tests that cross-build, so that may be where we add tests like this.

> Could this use the reading functionality available in System.Reflection.Metadata instead?

I think yes. I didn't know about `System.Reflection.Metadata`. I'm going to rewriting with `System.Reflection.Metadata`.

> Could this re-use that resource data model instead?

I think data model can be reused ~~but I think we need new writing resource logic because it looks current logic is for object file, not suitable for image files~~. writing logic may also reusable.
I have rewritten ResourceUpdater with System.Reflection.Metadata and Compiler/Win32Resources. Next, I'm going to write tests.

I've added minimum unit test.

For Integration tests, Is it should be in HostActivation.Tests and have an new TestProject with some resources?
I have merged master branch so I think Integration tests added by #89523 is included on this branch and it looks passed successfully.

> E2E tests for cross-building an app on Unix targeting Windows
> I believe the sdk repo has some tests that cross-build, so that may be where we add tests like this.

Sorry, I could not find cross-build tests in sdk repo.

These were the sdk tests I was thinking of:
https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/9c695f1661efd1b517d4a30900f0f4b2418bac97/src/Tests/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tests/GivenWeWantToRequireWindowsForDesktopApps.cs#L89-L118

Adding anything there would be a follow-up thing, since we'd need this to get in and flow over there.

I did pull this down and validate locally that I can patch the HostModel in a Linux install of the SDK and successfully build an app for Windows that gets an icon, manifest, copyright, and file version info.

Thank you for all the work and your responsiveness here!

Thanks for raising this PR. Drive-by question: cross-compiled WPF exe files end up with the wrong subsystem on the PE header. They end up with console UI instead of GUI. Will this PR fix this issue as well?
Thank you for suggesting the place for sdk tests.

> Thanks for raising this PR. Drive-by question: cross-compiled WPF exe files end up with the wrong subsystem on the PE header. They end up with console UI instead of GUI. Will this PR fix this issue as well?

Yes

This might also be fixing #88465 - would it be too much hassle to add a test case for this so we can close that bug too? It would exercise more of the resource rewriting logic. We're testing with this resource file here so I know it works with the ILCompiler logic, but might be nice to have a non-trivial test for this in AppHost as well: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/tests/nativeaot/SmokeTests/Win32Resources

> This might also be fixing #88465 - would it be too much hassle to add a test case for this so we can close that bug too?

Thank you, @anatawa12!

Thank you @anatawa12, that is awesome!

review_comments: Can you update the comments? It's no longer using an update handle / throwing InvalidOperation, since that was an artifact of how the Win32 APIs work.
This `Update` function depends on data in stream is same as `PEReader` created, so I think `Update` should throw `InvalidOperation` if Update() was already called instead of rewriting doc comments.

Could we switch the namespace to something like `Microsoft.NET.HostModel.Win32Resources` based on `#if HOST_MODEL` here?
Having HostModel define something in the ILCompiler namespace seems odd.
Can you switch this to return `type, name` instead of `name, type`? I find it confusing that the order is flipped from `AddResourceInternal`.

Umm... Old public function in `ResourceData`,`FindResource`, uses `name, type, language` order so I think it's better to change signature of `AddResource` and `AddResourceInternal`, and keep `name, type, language` order in GetAllResources.
Make this a `finally` instead of a `catch`, since it is always just rethrowing.
I think constructor of ResurceUpdater should dispose the stream if and only if exception ocurred. If constructor success, this.stream should be disposed later in `Dispose` method.
Ah, definitely. Bad reading on my part.
Can you also add ones with the same ushort type with different names?
I think these are all actually `type`, then `name` - that is the order for `AddResourceInternal`.
First I fixed the naming, and then swapped the parameters to match with FindResource.
I think this should be `CreateTestPEFileWithoutRsrc` - otherwise it will already have the resources we are trying to copy to it.
MemoryMappedViewAccessor has `ReadInt32` and overloads of `Write` for `int` and `short` that you should be able to use instead of having these helpers
It looks `ReadInt32` and `Write` uses native endianness instead of little endian so I reused helper function.

Nit: technically we should ifdef these out for ilc/crossgen - to avoid size bloat. But given that those two tools ships as AOTed images it will be trimmed away. Just wanted to point out that putting dead code in is not 100% free.

Can you please file an issue to move this code out of the "Compiler" directore and change the namespace such that we don't need the ifdefs everywhere.
I'm totally fine with it for this PR (let's not make it even bigger), but I personally don't like this, especially since it's in the same repo.
I filed #90063
Is there a reason we need to keep this method - as far as I can tell it only has two callsite in this same assembly.
There are some caller in sdk repository so I think we should keep this method for now. https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Adotnet%2Fsdk%20IsSupportedOS&type=code
Yeah, I think we can keep this so we don't break build when this flows. After this change flows to sdk, the usage in sdk can be removed and then this method itself.
